items.title: Aether Student Resiliency Framework
items.description: A structured approach to student support that connects wellbeing, learning habits, and clear intervention pathways.
items.question: How can a student-support framework make wellbeing, learning habits, and intervention pathways easier to discuss and improve?
items.method: Define needs, map support touchpoints, identify measurable signals, and turn the framework into a usable artifact.
items.evidence: Framework PDF, portfolio documentation, and support-center workflow.
items.outcome: A documented model for communicating the proposed support approach to mentors and collaborators.
items.limitation: This is a framework artifact, not a validated clinical or school-wide intervention study.
items.nextStep: Gather structured reviewer feedback and define an ethical, measurable pilot scope with an appropriate supervising adult or institution.

items.title: Research Notes to Shipped Features
items.description: A workflow for moving from early research notes into implementation decisions without losing academic rigor.
items.question: How can early research notes remain traceable when they become software decisions?
items.method: Use a hypothesis, prototype, validation, and reflection loop for each feature or project decision.
items.evidence: Published blog notes and reusable portfolio architecture.
items.outcome: A repeatable documentation pattern linking a decision to its published rationale and implementation context.
items.limitation: The workflow is an evolving personal practice; comparative effectiveness has not been formally measured.
items.nextStep: Publish a complete case study with a decision log, before-and-after artifact, and retrospective evaluation.

items.title: Modular Portfolio Architecture
items.description: A maintainable content system that keeps design blocks reusable while preserving a polished public experience.
items.question: Can a student portfolio remain editable, fast, and auditable as its research record grows?
items.method: Separate content JSON, Puck block contracts, shared UI components, metadata helpers, and tests.
items.evidence: Next.js app, shared-ui package, typed helpers, sitemap, robots, llms.txt, and structured data.
items.outcome: A version-controlled portfolio architecture with reusable components and an editor-facing content model.
items.limitation: The system has not yet been tested with a large body of publications or multiple independent editors.
items.nextStep: Add a full project case-study template and test the authoring workflow with an external reviewer.

props.heading: Academic Profile
props.body:
Aarti Sri Ravikumar is a student at Pioneer Charter School of Science II (PCSS-II) in Saugus, Massachusetts and the student social entrepreneur behind ai-aarti.com, a registered business.

Aarti’s work brings together research-informed software, clear technical writing, and systems that make learning and collaboration easier to navigate.

ai-aarti.com is a living record of that work. It gives mentors, educators, collaborators, and future reviewers a clear view of Aarti’s direction, evidence, and growth—without requiring them to piece together scattered links.

props.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
props.description: Short answers for mentors, collaborators, teachers, and search visitors.

faqs.question: What is the purpose of this portfolio?
faqs.answer: It presents Aarti Sri Ravikumar's direction, research-informed projects, writing, and collaboration pathways in one evidence-led website.

faqs.question: Where should a reviewer start?
faqs.answer: Start with How Aarti Turns Community Challenges into Action, then explore the method, research notes, and academic journey.

faqs.question: How can someone collaborate?
faqs.answer: Use the Support Center and include the project idea, scope, expected timeline, and relevant academic or technical context.

faqs.question: Is this portfolio built for search and AI discovery?
faqs.answer: Yes. It includes canonical metadata, structured data, sitemap generation, robots rules, llms.txt, share metadata, and content sections written for clear summarization.
